_comment: The burn assessment. This is a HUMAN act, not a computed value, which is why
it lives in a reviewed file in git rather than as a literal inside snapshot.mjs.
A refresh reads the chain and can say what supply and the treasury are RIGHT NOW.
It cannot say whether a burn was a JIP-38 burn — that needs attribution, and
attribution needs a person. So the refresh never advances this file. It compares
the chain against the anchor below and, if anything material has moved, marks the
published assessment 'review-required' instead of restamping it as freshly true.
To advance the assessment: re-do the attribution work, then update assessedAt,
burnedRaw, basis and the anchor together, in one reviewed commit.
basis: No JIP-38 burn found on chain by any method attempted. Jito stated on 2026-09-10 that no buybacks or burns had yet occurred. The absence is corroborated by the supply invariant: total destruction since genesis predates activation by a wide margin.

coverage.method: supply invariant plus targeted account enumeration
coverage.establishes: that no programme-scale burn appears in the accounts enumerated, and that total destruction since genesis is consistent with none
doesNotEstablish: that the enumerated accounts are all the accounts a JIP-38 burn could use
that fees were swept into JTO at all — the buyback step is untraced
the dates of the JTO destroyed before activation

anchor._comment: The chain state this assessment was made against. Movement away from it is what triggers review.
anchor.precisionNote: float-derived; recorded before exact base-unit accounting existed, so it is a trigger threshold rather than an exact quantity

reviewTriggers._comment: Any of these makes the published assessment 'review-required'.
